title: Cloud Sync setup
summary: Diceroll's Cloud Sync page, Setup tab: storage per player as the pkey.cloudSync.bytes entitlement (the platform default plus tier values, with players near each limit), what syncs read from the catalog, the per-product ceiling, the platform writes-paused switch, and the saves code.
compare: One page replaces the old read-only Data page: Cloud Sync in the sidebar with Setup and Usage tabs. The sidebar shows Diceroll's six features in canonical order (Licensing, Managed config, Ship builds, Sign-in, Cloud Sync, Commerce) with Sign-in on because Cloud Sync needs it. The page sub gives Verified per platform as status text, including "itch.io not seen yet" with the dashed ring.

Storage per player is the only quota: the Default row is the platform's registry default (256 MiB), marked with the Platform pill and "Every product, for people whose tier doesn't set it"; one row per tier with its own value or "Uses the default"; and players without a license, "Same as Free, the tier for players without a license". No by-tier, by-entitlement or unlicensed settings.

One action style in the column: a ghost Change on rows with their own value, Set where the tier uses the default, Change… on Default (it opens config.storage-default, the live platform default confirm), and Change in Access as a link for players without a license.

The card names the entitlement once (pkey.cloudSync.bytes) and links to Tiers, where the same value is edited. Near the limit is warning text only where it needs attention; the foot says when a change applies, that lowering it never deletes saves, and links to what players see when a save waits for room.

What syncs is read from the catalog (version named, Open Catalog): settings sync because they're Editable, with the count, the first keys, the ones that stay on each device and why, and settings the game adds itself (256 keys, 64 KiB).

Saves is the saves template (a neutral pill): slots, size, kept versions with "Older versions count toward the player's storage", the conflict rule in words (Ask the player), what the load screen shows, who can save, and one real slot.

Limits has exactly two controls: Diceroll's total storage (a meter, the platform default named, Change…) and Pause all Cloud Sync writes, marked Platform, off, with what it does and when it was last used; turning it on opens config.pause-writes. Limits and In your game share one row height.

In your game: "Settings sync with no extra code. Saves take one call.", GDScript first for Godot (then Swift for iOS, Kotlin for Android): config.set_value for a synced setting and cloud_sync.saves for a save with its metadata and the conflict signal.
A member with a product role only sees config.cloud-sync-product-role; while writes are paused the page is config.cloud-sync-paused.

Words: "player" for a game (Diceroll), "person" or "account" for an app (DJDL); storage in MiB and GiB, never MB; numbers and units never break across lines. products.integration's Cloud Sync card must say "Storage per person: 256 MiB by default (Standard uses the default)" to match this page.
No word "Data" for this page, no access classes, no conflict-mode jargon (lastWrite, revision) and no save-slot setting.
Phone: the tier table becomes one block per row, the What syncs panes stack, the Platform pill sits on its own line under the switch's title, and the code tabs scroll sideways with a fading edge.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the platform default is marked and confirmed like one, the actions agree, and the copy, Verified line and layout are corrected.

findings.issue: Change on the Default row edited the platform-wide 256 MiB default with no Platform marking and no confirm naming the products it affects.
findings.resolution: The row carries the Platform pill and reads "Every product, for people whose tier doesn't set it"; Change… opens ST-16's live platform default confirm, drawn as config.storage-default, which names DJDL and Diceroll with who uses the default in each and confirms with a passkey.

findings.issue: Four action treatments in one column (outline, pencil, text Set, nothing).
findings.resolution: One ghost style: Change on rows with their own value, Set on Standard (uses the default), Change… on Default, and Change in Access as a link on players without a license.

findings.issue: "Anonymous devices tier (Free)" read like a second tier or a price, with no way to change it.
findings.resolution: "Same as Free, the tier for players without a license" with Change in Access.

findings.issue: "Settings need no code" sat above code that calls set_value.
findings.resolution: "Settings sync with no extra code. Saves take one call."

findings.issue: The Verified line left out itch.io.
findings.resolution: The page sub adds "itch.io not seen yet" as muted status with the dashed ring, the products.integration pattern; config.cloud-sync-usage shows it too.

findings.issue: It never said whether kept versions count toward storage or what a player sees at the limit.
findings.resolution: Keeps adds "Older versions count toward the player's storage."; the card foot links "What players see then".

findings.issue: Ragged bottom row, a floating Platform pill and cut code tabs on phone, and "64 KiB" breaking.
findings.resolution: Limits and In your game stretch to one row height; on phone the pill has its own line and the tabs scroll with a fading edge; numbers and units are joined by non-breaking spaces.

findings.issue: No state for a member with a product role only.
findings.resolution: Added config.cloud-sync-product-role: Change… on Default and the pause switch are disabled, each with "Only platform admins …".

findings.issue: products.integration's DJDL card contradicts this page's storage model and uses MB.
findings.resolution: Not changed here, as the finding says: the fix belongs to products.integration, another designer's screen, and goes to the lead to route. The naming and unit rule is now in this screen's compare list.
